priorities.finding: Request context is the only train-only screened group with positive primary lift (+0.00221) and full coverage, but its lift is small relative to daily variability (0.00580). The tab-by-hour interaction did not validate: experiment 2 primary (0.602885) was lower than experiment 1 (0.602935).
priorities.recommended_action: Apply strict early stopping: do not fund another feature or interaction experiment. Retain the existing leakage-safe request-context treatment only if it is already in the scorer; require a new independently justified hypothesis and stronger train-only within-user ranking evidence before reopening experimentation.

priorities.finding: The main weakness is top-five ranking in specific tab slices, not a uniform loss of within-user discrimination. Tab 5 has GAUC 0.25 and nDCG@5 0.1063; tab 8 has GAUC 0.3889 and nDCG@5 0.0265. Tab 0 is also materially weak at nDCG@5 0.0627 despite GAUC 0.5597. Rare items are weak at nDCG@5 0.1717, although their small sample limits confidence.
priorities.recommended_action: Treat these as post-score diagnostic targets rather than evidence for immediate feature spend. If experimentation resumes, pre-register a leakage-safe, tab-specific candidate-generation or ranking hypothesis and evaluate GAUC and nDCG@5 separately; do not infer improved top-five ranking from GAUC alone.

avoid: Do not use current-impression outcome fields, including click, like, follow, comment, long-view, play-time, or stay-time signals, as ranking features.
Do not use aggregate video-statistic snapshot fields without per-impression availability timestamps.
Do not revive rejected train-only groups: user_profile, historical_user_author_affinity, upload_recency, content_duration, item_metadata, historical_author_response, or historical_item_response.
Do not optimize against user_positive_count slices; they use validation labels only for retrospective diagnostics.
metric_diagnosis: Experiment 2 has solid aggregate within-user ranking discrimination (GAUC 0.66919) but no validated primary improvement over experiment 1, so aggregate GAUC is insufficient to justify additional budget. Its primary is driven down by concentrated top-five failures in tabs 5, 8, and 0, where nDCG@5 is much weaker than global nDCG@5 0.53658. Zero-positive users have nDCG@5 of 0 by construction and are not a model-ranking failure. Evidence: experiment:2:metrics, experiment:2:segment:tab:5, experiment:2:segment:tab:8, experiment:2:segment:tab:0, experiment:2:segment:user_positive_count:zero.
